note: Selective JAK2 inhibitors (not ruxolitinib): fedratinib approved 2019 on JAKARTA spleen response with a Wernicke's encephalopathy boxed warning; NS-018 (ilginatinib) and BMS-911543 stopped after phase 1/2 for business reasons.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Cancer Cell, Europe PMC). Quote is the first 36 words of a longer sentence.
engagement.note: Fedratinib (TG101348) cut pSTAT5 and JAK2V617F disease burden in the mouse model; no patient data yet.

engagement.short: Allele burden fell, less than mice
engagement.quote: A significant decrease in JAK2 V617F allele burden was observed at 6 months in mutation-positive patients (n = 51; P = .04), particularly in the subgroup with allele burden greater than 20% (n = 23; P < .01)

engagement.quote: Fedratinib inhibited cytokine-induced STAT3 phosphorylation in whole blood from patients with myelofibrosis.

dose.judgement: The mouse's lack of toxicity is not a stated margin at a human-relevant exposure, so dose stays untested.
dose.note: Mouse efficacy at 60-120 mg/kg twice daily; no human exposure target or tolerability margin was stated from the model.
dose.quote: There were no apparent toxicities and no effect on T cell number.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA review NDA 212327 restates the mouse data (splenomegaly, fibrosis, survival).
efficacy.note: Fedratinib shrank extramedullary hematopoiesis (spleen) and attenuated fibrosis in JAK2V617F mice.
efficacy.quote: In treated animals, there was a statistically significant reduction in hematocrit and leukocyte count, a dose-dependent reduction/elimination of extramedullary hematopoiesis, and, at least in some instances, evidence for attenuation of myelofibrosis.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: spleen reduction: mouse extramedullary hematopoiesis vs patient SVR35 rate
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read; NCT01437787 results first posted 2026-08-11 per ClinicalTrials.gov. The FDA review (2019) relies on the same primary endpoint.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: JAKARTA reports no mouse data. The model is a PV-like V617F transplant model, scored for MF because it was the cited efficacy model in the FDA review. NS-018 and BMS-911543 on this system are their own tracks, appended at the end of this cell.
efficacy.note: JAKARTA: 36-40% on fedratinib vs 1% on placebo reached the primary 35% spleen-volume reduction, as the mouse predicted.
efficacy.quote: The primary end point was achieved by 35 of 96 (36% [95% CI, 27%-46%]) and 39 of 97 (40% [95% CI, 30%-50%]) patients in the fedratinib 400-mg and 500-mg groups, vs 1 of 96

patient_trials.quote: By six and 12 cycles of treatment, 39% and 47% of patients, respectively, had achieved a spleen response per International Working Group criteria.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read; cells were PV, not MF, progenitors.

efficacy.quote: Thus, TG101348 may be an effective inhibitor of JAK2V617F+ MPDs in clinical trials.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived JAK2V617F+ progenitor colonies and xenograft (TG101348)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstracts read; NCT01437787 results first posted 2026-08-11. PV progenitors scored for MF patients.

efficacy.quote: The primary end point was achieved by 35 of 96 (36% [95% CI, 27%-46%]) and 39 of 97 (40% [95% CI, 30%-50%]) patients in the fedratinib 400-mg and 500-mg groups, vs 1 of 96
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; JAKARTA cites no ex-vivo data. BMS-911543 on patient CD34+ progenitors (Purandare 2012) is its own track, appended at the end of this cell.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived JAK2V617F+ progenitor colonies and xenograft (TG101348)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Phase 1 (Verstovsek 2017) primary objective was safety; NCT01423851 Part 2 (prior-JAKi patients) posted 1/12 IWG-MRT/ELN responders and a mean spleen-volume fall in 2022 with no author verdict or quotable sentence; phase 2b NCT04854096 was terminated (business) with 0 SVR35 responders in 5 vs 2 patients.
efficacy.judgement: Post-dating: this model result was public after fedratinib's phase 1 spleen responses (Pardanani 2011), a patient result for the same target and action. Split from the fedratinib entry (efficacy 2): NS-018 is its own track. No quotable primary-endpoint result, so untested. Flagged retrodiction on its scored entry only, as an untested opener compares nothing.
efficacy.note: NS-018 (ilginatinib) cut splenomegaly and marrow fibrosis in this mouse. Its single-arm phase 1/2 patient data give no scorable primary efficacy result.
efficacy.short: NS-018 mice: spleen and fibrosis improved
efficacy.quote: in a JAK2V617F bone marrow transplantation mouse model with a myelofibrosis-like disease, NS-018 reduced leukocytosis and splenomegaly, improved bone marrow fibrosis and prolonged survival without decreasing the erythrocyte or PLT count in the peripheral blood

patient_trials.quote: A ⩾50% reduction in palpable spleen size was achieved in 56% of patients (47% of patients with prior JAKi treatment), and improvements were observed in myelofibrosis-associated symptoms.

efficacy.judgement: Post-dating: this model result was public after fedratinib's phase 1 spleen responses (Pardanani 2011), a patient result for the same target and action. Opening entry for the BMS-911543 track at its first use on this system. Flagged retrodiction on its scored entry only, as an untested opener compares nothing.
efficacy.note: BMS-911543 normalised white counts but left red cells and the JAK2V617F clone unchanged in this mouse; the authors called its activity limited.
efficacy.quote: Collectively, these results show that BMS-911543 has limited activity in this murine model of JAK2(V617F)-driven MPN and suggest that targeting JAK2 alone may be insufficient to achieve effective disease control.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: limited activity in mice vs IWG-MRT clinical improvement or remission in 24/42 phase II patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results (NCT01236352, posted 2019-05-21) set the year; Tefferi 2023 abstract quoted (BMS-911543 is the fourth of the listed cohorts). Programme stopped for business reasons; remissions were few.
efficacy.judgement: Single-arm ruling: a response where the model predicted little is contra. A failed retrodiction, since the mouse result post-dated fedratinib's spleen responses. Low confidence because 'limited' was relative and most responses were clinical improvement, not remission.
efficacy.note: Patients on BMS-911543 responded where the mouse predicted limited activity. Design: NCT01236352 was a non-randomized phase 1/2 trial with no success bar set in advance, scored on its primary IWG-MRT best overall response: in phase II, 3/42 partial remissions and 21/42 clinical improvements (results posted 2019-05-21); Mayo's 31 patients had a 62% spleen response.
efficacy.quote: Using conventional criteria, the respective response rates for spleen and "transfusion-dependent anemia" were 47%, 32%, 83%, 62% and 51%, 30%, 10%, 44%, respectively, favoring momelotinib for anemia response (p = 0.02) and fedratinib for spleen response (p < 0.01).

safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the IND opened October 2007, so the IND-enabling toxicology predates it; the data were public only in the 2019 review.
safety.note: Rat and dog repeat-dose studies named marrow, GI and liver as target organs; no CNS findings of note. Gait abnormalities were seen in high-dose animals.
safety.quote: There were no clear drug-related CNS effects in rats; eye miosis and lack of pupillary responses were observed but were non-dose-dependent.

safety.note: Mouse studies reported no apparent toxicities for fedratinib; a passing tolerability claim, scored as this model's safety prediction.
safety.quote: There were no apparent toxicities and no effect on T cell number.

safety.magnitude_basis: red cell and platelet counts: unchanged in mice vs drug-related cytopenias in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. Model side quote (Nakaya 2014): 'NS-018 reduced leukocytosis and splenomegaly, improved bone marrow fibrosis and prolonged survival without decreasing the erythrocyte or PLT count'. Registry date is NCT01423851 results posting. The NS-018 safety track opens on this entry: its 2014 opener could not be appended after it without breaking year order.
safety.judgement: The NS-018 paper stated a named on-target sparing (no fall in erythrocytes or platelets) that patients contradicted; scored contra. Thrombocytopenia in MF patients is partly disease-related, but these were called drug-related. Fedratinib's 2011 grade 3-4 anemia/thrombocytopenia was not scored against Wernig, since the hematocrit fall was that model's efficacy readout and platelet data were not seen at abstract level.
safety.note: NS-018 mice kept red cell and platelet counts; in phase 1 patients thrombocytopenia (27%) and anemia (15%) were the commonest drug-related events. Phase 1 was a single-arm dose escalation.
safety.quote: The most common drug-related adverse events were thrombocytopenia (27%)/anemia (15%) for hematologic events, and dizziness (23%)/nausea (19%) for non-hematologic events.
safety.reason: Cytopenias the mouse said NS-018 spared

safety.magnitude_basis: CNS/thiamine-deficiency harm absent in animals, present in patients
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text read (bundle). JAKARTA (2015) first reported the WE cases; the clinical hold was November 2013. A post-hoc 28-day rat study found no thiamine change but reached only 0.3-fold human AUC, so it neither reproduces nor clears the signal.
safety.judgement: Scored as a harm the species could show (rats develop thiamine-deficiency encephalopathy), although fedratinib's causal role in thiamine depletion remains debated in the review. The anemia, thrombocytopenia, GI and liver-enzyme findings the toxicology predicted did appear in patients; one contra outranks them on the track.
safety.note: Patients developed encephalopathy including Wernicke's (boxed warning) that the rat and dog studies had not shown; predicted marrow and GI toxicity held.
safety.quote: Encephalopathy, including Wernicke’s encephalopathy (a life‐threatening illness caused by thiamine deficiency), occurred in 7/608 (1.2%) of patients who received 500 mg of fedratinib in clinical trials.
safety.reason: Encephalopathy not seen in rat or dog

safety.confidence_note: Abstract read; retrodiction flag sits on the scored entry.
safety.note: Caco-2 and recombinant human thiamine transporter assays built after the Wernicke's cases to probe fedratinib's effect on thiamine uptake.
safety.quote: Transport studies with recombinant human thiamine transporters identified the individual human thiamine transporter (hTHTR2) that is inhibited by fedratinib.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use; run after the 2013 clinical hold.
safety.model: Caco-2 and recombinant hTHTR2 thiamine-uptake assay

safety.magnitude_basis: thiamine-uptake inhibition vs WE in 8/608 patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract read (full text paywalled). Fedratinib's causal role in WE remains debated in the FDA review.
safety.note: Fedratinib potently inhibited thiamine uptake via hTHTR2, reproducing the thiamine-deficiency encephalopathy seen in patients after the fact.
safety.quote: In vitro studies indicate that fedratinib potently inhibits the carrier-mediated uptake and transcellular flux of thiamine in Caco-2 cells, suggesting that oral absorption of dietary thiamine is significantly compromised by fedratinib dosing.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the paper opens by citing the WE cases; the sponsor's own transporter assay (separate track) disagreed.
safety.model: Caco-2 and recombinant hTHTR2 thiamine-uptake assay

safety.confidence_note: FDA review text in bundle; study year from its code.
safety.note: Sponsor tested fedratinib on ThTr1/ThTr2 in MDCK-II monolayers after the WE cases (study OPT-2017-097); public only in 2019.
safety.quote: Fedratinib was tested from 1 to 300 μM using polarized monolayer of Madin Darby Canine Kidney (MDCK)‐11 cells expressing ThTr1 or ThTr2.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use (proxy year from study code).

safety.magnitude_basis: ThTr inhibition at clinical exposure vs WE in 7/608 patients
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text in bundle. The review itself is equivocal on whether fedratinib causes thiamine depletion; Zhang 2014 reported potent hTHTR2 inhibition.
safety.note: Assay found weak ThTr inhibition only at ~100-fold clinical Cmax, failing to reproduce the encephalopathy patients had.
safety.short: Assay missed thiamine harm post hoc
safety.quote: Fedratinib in vitro inhibition of ThTr1 and ThTr2 was 24.5% and 44.2%, respectively, at 300 μM (about 100‐fold the Cmax in patients at the recommended daily dose of 400 mg).
safety.judgement: Failed retrodiction scored contra; low confidence because the human harm's drug causality is debated.
safety.reason: Weak inhibition, harm seen in patients

safety.magnitude_basis: no apparent toxicity in mice vs grade 3-4 GI events 3-10% and cytopenias in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract read. Anemia was the model's own efficacy readout (hematocrit fell), so not a miss; platelet data in mice not seen at abstract level.
safety.judgement: Partial: the authors' call matches, but GI and hematologic grade 3-4 events show the mouse claim was not complete. Wernicke's encephalopathy (2013) is scored on the rat/dog toxicology track, not here: a short mouse efficacy study on thiamine-replete chow is not one that could show it.
safety.note: Phase 1 authors called fedratinib well tolerated, as the mouse's 'no apparent toxicities' claim stated; grade 3-4 diarrhoea (10%), anemia (35%) and thrombocytopenia (24%) occurred. Scored under the ruling that a passing tolerability claim is a safety prediction.
safety.short: Tolerated in patients, as mice showed
safety.quote: TG101348 is well tolerated and produces significant reduction in disease burden and durable clinical benefit in patients with myelofibrosis.
